newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC expects record 1996 wheat crop in France.
newsitem.headline: ONIC expects record 1996 wheat crop in France.

text.p: French cereals office ONIC confirmed on Wednesday it was expecting France to harvest a record soft wheat crop of 33.8 million tonnes in 1996, exceeding previous record highs of 32.65 million in 1984 and 32.05 million in 1991.

ONIC's estimate, the first since the harvest got under way in July, also sees the 1996 barley crop at 9.36 million tonnes against 7.74 million in 1995 and a maize crop of 13.6 million against 12.4 million in 1995.
The wheat crop estimate assumes the national yield would rise to a record 7.07 tonnes per hectare from 6.60 tonnes in 1995. The previous record for soft wheat yield was 6.82 tonnes reached in 1991.
Soft wheat area is seen rising to 4.78 million hectares from 4.52 million.
ONIC also forecast barley yields would rise to 6.18 tonnes per hectare from 5.56 tonnes in 1995 and area to 1.513 million hectares from 1.393 million.
Maize area was forecast at 1.7 million hectares against 1.62 million in 1995 and yields at 8.0 tonnes per hectare against 7.64 tonnes in 1995.
French wheat growers association AGPB is eyeing a soft wheat crop of 34 million tonnes.
The French farm ministry has raised its estimate for the 1996 grain harvest to 61 million tonnes from a previous target of 57.3 million, grain industry sources said on Tuesday.
The ministry is expected to officially release the figures later this week.
The ministry now targets a soft wheat crop of 34.1 million tonnes, a barley crop of 9.3 million and a maize crop of 13.8 million tonnes.
